newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka Bank of Ceylon opens second Nepal branch.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka Bank of Ceylon opens second Nepal branch.

text.p: Sri Lanka's state-owned Bank of Ceylon opened its seventh foreign branch on Monday, in Nepal, a bank official said on Tuesday.
"This is the second branch in Nepal, and this time it is in Kathmandu," the official told Reuters.
The bank opened its first Nepal branch in Siddarthanagar, near Lumbini, the birthplace of Buddha, in October 1996.
The Bank of Ceylon, Sri Lanka's largest commercial bank, also has two branches in London, and one each in Male in the Maldives, Karachi in Pakistan and Madras in India.
A branch in Moscow was also on the cards for 1997, the official said.
Overseas branches, which proved very profitable, have contributed significantly towards improved earnings, he added.
Unaudited pre-tax profits of the bank for the financial year to 31 December 1996, rose to 3.2 billion rupees, from 2.8 billion in 1995.
